editorial:
You know that feeling when a movie grabs you in the first five minutes and never lets go? That is exactly what happens here. Halle Berry plays Jordan Turner, a seasoned 911 operator who is still shaken after a past call went horribly wrong. When a teenager named Casey gets snatched and locked in the trunk of a car, Jordan is the voice on the other end of the line. The whole movie plays out like a tense phone call stretched into a full thriller, and it works surprisingly well. You feel every second of Casey's fear and Jordan's determination to keep her alive.

The pacing is tight and rarely slows down, which keeps you on the edge of your seat. Berry is fantastic, and Abigail Breslin sells the terror of being trapped. The movie does stumble a bit near the end when it shifts from smart thriller to something more like a revenge story, but the ride there is so gripping you will not mind much. If you love tense, fast-moving crime thrillers, this one is a great pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture and sound.
endingExplained: Jordan figures out the kidnapper is Michael Foster, a man who lost his sister years ago and now targets girls who look like her. She tracks him to an abandoned house and finds Casey locked in a basement. Instead of waiting for police, Jordan frees Casey and the two trap Michael in a hidden room. They lock him inside and leave, letting him suffer the same fate he planned for his victims. It is a dark, satisfying twist that turns the victim into the one in control.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves tense crime thrillers and strong female leads.
